claims.ready_paraphrase: Born in Puranagarh in1916, Gopal Chhotray made Cuttack the centre of a working life that crossed theatre, broadcasting and cinema. His archive contains plays, stories, translations and unpublished scripts. The variety offers a way into his work beyond a single medium.

claims.ready_paraphrase: A1957 radio notice introduces a playwright who has found fame by turning a young woman’s life into drama. Then it turns attention back to her. The play was Sova, by Gopal Chhotray, scheduled on AIR Cuttack for8April. Even this brief announcement opens a question about whose life becomes a story—and who benefits.

claims.ready_paraphrase: The Library of Congress preserves readings from Pheria, Parakalama and Sei phula. They offer something a film credit cannot: a route to the author’s own voice. Its catalogue also keeps publication history visible, separating later editions from the earlier appearance of the works.
Hasyarasara Natak received the Sahitya Akademi award in1982. The award recognised dramatic writing; it should not be confused with a film honour.
For Maa, Gopal shared the dialogue credit with Biswajit Das; Nitai Palit handled screenplay and direction. The distinctions make the collaboration visible.
His dialogue work for Sri Jagannath places him in the early history of Odia filmmaking, alongside C.R. Mitra’s direction and screenplay.
